Question: For people involved in the streets, is not snitching on another criminal to the cops really worth the extra time in jail or prison?
Answer: Question: For people involved in the streets, is not snitching on another criminal to the cops really worth the extra time in jail or prison? Normally,no. Snitching is like teenaged sex: Nearly everybody does it, they just don’t want to make a big deal about it. Things get grim when people get arrested. Many cannot afford lawyers, they already have warrants out for their arrest for other offenses besides what they have been arrested for this time, some are on parole or probation; and some are repeat customers which in some states can trigger “habitual offender” sentencing guidelines which can mean 25 or more years for any felony offense. Basically they are starting off in a bad position and not snitching and stick to that stance is not going to go well for them. Additionally, if they have criminal accomplices or even if they have told someone who themselves is facing criminal prosecution for something else, they have to hope that person keeps the faith. You may not snitch; however if others were there or know as much as you do and they don’t want to go to prison for long, if at all, they are going to speak up. You can be a standup guy all you want, but that simply means that you’ll take most or all of the weight for the crime. Finally, most criminals have never been to a maximum security prison or have only served minor sentences in lower security facilities or jails. When faced with possibility of spending decades, if not the remainder of their lives in a real hellhole, that tends to loosen tongues. Most criminal organizations either don’t have the financial capability to make hanging tough worth their members while; or they are run by greedy and short-term who don’t think that they need to do so. After a few months in jail or a few years in prison, many people decide that they want a shorter sentence, a transfer to a better facility, or even a release from incarceration. So while “Snitches get stitches” gets bandied about in the streets, the reality nearly everyone tries to what best for themselves. It’s rare that sitting in prison and taking most or the full weight for criminal offenses is consistent with that stance. To expect people to remain silent is mostly a fantasy buoyed along by the media rather than a reflection of objective realities.
